title: Book One · Chapter 94: One Mark Without a Name
story:
There is a tick on the page. What does the tick mean? Nobody knows.

“Perhaps three stones,” Mei says. “Perhaps two,” Ronan says. “I think it is for my boat,” Leo says. His group borrowed that corner of the desk.

“It is on our page,” Ronan says.

“Your page was under ours.”

They look at the little black mark. It has no number beside it. There is no name above it. A small wet patch dried across the line below.

Miss Wu asks them to choose the results for the class book. Ronan wants a three-stone result in the class book. But this mark needs a clear meaning first.

“Perhaps it is three,” Ronan says.

Mei shakes her head. “Perhaps is not a number.”

“You said three before.”

“I said I thought so.”

They take the page to Miss Wu. She cannot remember the mark. The children cannot remember it either.

“Then we leave it out of the results,” she says.

Ronan looks down at the page. He wanted to keep that result. “But someone did it.”

“Yes. But the mark has no clear meaning.”

He goes back to the table. Leo has drawn a question mark beside the tick. Mei does not rub either out.

“Can we test again?” Ronan asks.

Their old flat boat is still firm and whole. The paper boat is too soft now. They cannot test it again in the same way. The paste boat needs checking after its last use.

Miss Wu gives them time at the lesson's end. They can do one careful test. They choose the flat wooden boat. They can use the same wood and stones again.

This time they write on the page first. They write the date, boat letter and test number. Then they put the boat in the water. Mei makes a little space for each result. Ronan says the result aloud. Leo watches. His hands stay off the boat.

The boat carries three stones in the middle again. It tips with two at the front again.

Now the new mark has a name and a number. The old tick stays in the folder, with the question mark beside it.

Mei makes a key at the bottom of the page. This list helps them read the marks. A circle means empty. A tick means still floating at the end of the test. A cross means tipped or sank. They write tipped or sank beside the cross.

Ronan reads the key slowly. One cross can say two things. He asks her to separate tipped from sank. They make two different marks instead of one.

At home, Mum is checking her sewing notes. One line says blue. But there are two blue shirts in Mum's basket.

Ronan notices her stop. He does not rush to say she made the same mistake as his group. Mum is already taking out both shirts. She compares them with the names on their tags.

“Would a number help?” he asks.

“Next time, perhaps. These names will do today.”

He helps her put the shirts in separate piles. Mum can check her own notes. Ronan can help her with the shirt piles. She needs the right name for each shirt. Now he understands the careful checking.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- tick＝勾号
- test again＝再次测试
- key＝图例
- separate＝分开

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：tag＝标签；folder＝文件夹；aloud＝出声地。

## 读句提示

**They write the date, boat letter and test number.**

他们／写下／日期、船的字母标记、测试编号。先写，再下水。

## 理解问题

1. 为什么一个看似有利的勾号也不能直接使用？
2. 新的记录方式补上了哪些信息？
